as_written_in_papers.quote: Two compound heterozygous variants, c.265_267del (p.Ile89del) and c.253G>T (p.Glu85*), of the GAMT gene were identified (Figure 1B).

cases.statement: One person: a 52-year-old Taiwanese woman (index case of 42885896), compound heterozygous for c.253G>T (p.Glu85*) and c.265_267del (p.Ile89del), phased in trans from sequencing reads.

people.label: Our case (Table 1 #1)
people.zygosity_or_genotype: compound heterozygous (in trans by read phasing)
people.key_phenotypes: neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy with atonic seizures, developmental delay and intellectual disability, dystonia and ataxia, orolingual dyskinesia, absent creatine peak on brain MRS

quotes.quote: We present a 52‐year‐old female with a history of neonatal‐onset epileptic encephalopathy, developmental delay, intellectual disability, dystonia, and ataxia.
At age 51, she was referred to our outpatient clinic due to functional decline accompanied by increased atonic seizures
Clinical examination revealed involuntary movements involving the tongue, characteristic of orolingual dyskinesia.
Biochemical workup revealed a low serum creatinine level (0.24 mg/dL), while brain MRS demonstrated an absent or diminished creatine signal in the left thalamus and basal ganglia (Figure 3).
One month later, the patient became completely seizure‐free

phenotype_specificity.statement: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with movement disorder, low serum creatinine and absent/diminished brain creatine on MRS, and seizure freedom after creatine. Plasma/DBS GAA was not measured. WES was interpreted with epilepsy and rare-disease panels; two further variants in ALPL and POLG were judged unrelated.

quotes.quote: We present a 52‐year‐old female with a history of neonatal‐onset epileptic encephalopathy, developmental delay, intellectual disability, dystonia, and ataxia.
Biochemical workup revealed a low serum creatinine level (0.24 mg/dL), while brain MRS demonstrated an absent or diminished creatine signal in the left thalamus and basal ganglia (Figure 3).
First, the plasma or dried blood spot GAA measurement was not obtained because it was locally unavailable.

Nevertheless, the diagnosis of GAMT deficiency was established by compound heterozygous likely pathogenic GAMT variants, marked depletion of cerebral creatine on brain MRS, a phenotype concordant with DEE, and clear clinical improvement following creatine supplementation.
To correlate with the patient's phenotype (epilepsy and developmental delay), clinical interpretation focused on an epilepsy panel (1045 genes) and a rare disease panel (7452 genes).
WES identified 4 variants: 2 variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in the ALPL and POLG genes, which were considered unrelated to the patient's phenotype.

segregation.statement: Not reported. No family history of a similar condition; no relatives are reported as tested.

quotes.quote: There was no family history of a similar condition (Figure 1A).

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.265_267del (p.Ile89del). Phase was shown directly from WES reads in IGV (the variants are close together), not by parental testing.

quotes.quote: Two compound heterozygous variants, c.265_267del (p.Ile89del) and c.253G>T (p.Glu85*), of the GAMT gene were identified (Figure 1B).

Furthermore, because the genomic locations of these two variants are in close proximity, we were able to directly phase the sequencing reads using the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV), which confirmed their in trans (compound heterozygous) configuration.
The alignment highlights a compound heterozygous state in the GAMT gene, comprising a single amino acid deletion c.265_267del (p.Ile89del) and a nonsense mutation c.253G>T (p.Glu85*).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense change, predicted p.(Glu85Ter) (from the HGVS). The authors call it a null variant. No further mechanism statement specific to this variant.

Similarly, the c.253G>T variant fulfills the criteria for PVS1 (null variant), PM2_supporting (rare in population databases), and PM3 (in trans), supporting its final classification of “likely pathogenic” for c.253G>T.

computational_predictions.statement: not reported for this variant. The methods list in-silico tools used in general, but no scores for c.253G>T are given (cohort-level methods statement).

quotes.quote: The impacts of variants on protein function were evaluated using multiple in silico prediction tools (e.g., AlphaMissense, CADD, REVEL, and SpliceAI).

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors cite PM2_supporting ('rare in population databases') without numbers, and state the variant has not yet been reported in ClinVar.

Currently, the c.265_267del variant is classified as a VUS in the ClinVar database, whereas the c.253G>T variant has not yet been reported.

concerns: Other candidate variants in the same person: WES also found two variants in ALPL and POLG, which the authors considered unrelated to the phenotype.

The paper contradicts itself on novelty of the other allele: the abstract calls both c.265_267del and c.253G>T 'novel', while the case report says c.265_267del was previously reported in a homozygous patient.
Phase was established from sequencing reads, not from parents; no relatives were tested.
GAA was not measured, so the biochemical diagnosis rests on low serum creatinine and MRS.
The authors' in-trans criterion rests on the other allele c.265_267del, whose own database status the paper quotes as uncertain.
notes_for_panel: Single adult case with strong clinical-biochemical (MRS) support and a reported dramatic response to creatine. 42885896 Table S1 #84 lists c.265_267delATC (the other allele) in a different patient (Passi 2022 Pt 9); that row does not involve c.253G>T.
